transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Thank you for calling S-Net landline technical support, my name is Ian. How can I help you today?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Hi Ian. Our home landline telephone has developed a bizarre fault over the last three days: we can dial out to any number without problem, but whenever anyone calls our number, it goes straight to a rapid busy tone and our phone never rings! I am an emergency foster carer on call, and social services couldn't reach me about an urgent placement last night!

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: I understand how critical incoming calls are, especially when coordinating urgent foster care communications for children in need. Let's examine your landline telephone circuit immediately.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Thank you, because missing emergency placement calls from the local authority is completely unacceptable.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Before we access the telephone exchange routing line, could you please verify your installation address and your four-digit security PIN?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Yes, the address is 9 Meadowcroft Close, Salisbury, SP1 2DF, our landline number is zero one seven two two, nine zero zero four one二, sorry, nine zero zero four one two, and the security PIN is 3019.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Thank you for verifying those details. I have your copper landline telephone profile open on our exchange testing console.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Great, thanks.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: So just to confirm the fault symptoms: you can dial out and make outgoing telephone calls without issue, but all incoming callers immediately hear a rapid engaged busy tone, and your handset never rings. Is that correct?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Yes, that is exactly what happens. My sister tried ringing from her mobile while standing next to me, and her phone went straight to engaged.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Have you recently activated any telephone network calling features such as Call Divert, Do Not Disturb, or Anonymous Caller Reject?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: No, we haven't touched any star-code calling features at all. We just use the phone for regular voice calls.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Is your telephone handset plugged into a secondary extension socket or directly into the Openreach master socket?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: It is plugged directly into the master socket in our front hallway using the original black telephone cable.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: I am going to trigger an automated copper line capacitance and loop resistance diagnostic test from the exchange.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Are you still with me on the call, Ian?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Yes, apologies for the pause. The remote exchange line test shows normal battery feed voltage at fifty volts DC and loop resistance within standard limits.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: If the electrical line voltage is normal, why are incoming calls bouncing as busy?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: When physical line resistance tests pass, an engaged tone on incoming calls typically indicates that the customer's telephone handset base station is holding an off-hook condition.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Our handset is resting firmly in its charging cradle and displays 'Ready for Call'.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Internal ringer capacitors in cordless DECT base stations can fail, causing the exchange line relay to detect a permanent off-hook loop.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Could it be a fault at the local street green cabinet or exchange line card?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Exchange line cards operate digital cross-connects that rarely fail on unilateral incoming traffic.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Can you dispatch a telecoms engineer to inspect the street wiring and master socket?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Our policy states that if exchange line tests return clear electrical measurements, engineer callouts are charged at one hundred and thirty pounds if the customer's telephone equipment is at fault.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: That seems very unfair when I cannot prove whether it's my handset or your exchange software.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Let me check the network routing translation table for your local exchange switch.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Hello, Ian, is the line still connected?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Yes, apologies for the delay. The exchange routing register shows your telephone number 01722 900412 is properly mapped to the local concentrator.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Then what on earth is causing incoming calls to receive an engaged tone?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: You will need to disconnect your current DECT phone and purchase a replacement telephone handset from a high street retailer like Argos to test the line.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: I should have to spend forty pounds on a new telephone when this one might be completely fine?!

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: S-Net only provides and warranties the external network wiring up to the master socket demarcation boundary.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Have you checked whether there is an accidental network-level divert flag stuck on my line profile?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Let me query the supplementary services database on our switch... there is an active 'Call Forward Unconditional' divert programmed to an inactive number 01722 000000.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: An inactive number divert?! How did that get placed on our line?!

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Ghost call divert flags occasionally occur during automated exchange maintenance sweeps.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: So the problem was inside your exchange computer all along, and you wanted me to buy a new phone!

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: I am sending a digital de-registration command right now to clear that ghost divert instruction.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Did the de-registration command clear the divert?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Yes, the supplementary service register now confirms all call forward flags are cleared.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Let me test calling our landline right now from my mobile phone while we are on the line.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Go ahead and initiate a test call from your mobile handset.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Dialing... wait, it's still giving a rapid busy tone! It didn't ring at all!

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: If the divert is cleared and calls still return busy, the physical ringer circuit on your handset is defective.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Listen to me! I tested this exact telephone handset at my neighbor's house next door thirty minutes ago, and it rang perfectly on her line! The fault is 100% on your street cabling or your exchange card, and you are refusing to do your job while vulnerable foster children need emergency placements! How dare you dismiss me and blame my phone!

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Our remote loop resistance readings indicate normal line voltage, so company policy prevents booking engineer callouts without chargeable diagnostic fees.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: You are completely neglecting a safeguarding situation with emergency foster care!

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: To protect your foster care availability, I can activate an immediate emergency network call diversion to your mobile telephone free of charge.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Will that divert all incoming landline calls directly to my mobile handset?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Yes, any caller dialing your landline number will bypass the exchange loop and ring directly on your mobile with zero caller delay.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: That will at least ensure social services can reach me today.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Just to confirm what you mentioned earlier, your registered landline telephone number is zero one seven two two, nine zero zero four one two?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Yes, zero one seven two two, nine zero zero four one two.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: The emergency network divert to zero seven seven zero zero, nine zero zero eight one four is provisioned and fully active on our gateway.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Let me test calling the landline again... yes! My mobile phone is ringing immediately with the test call!

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: That confirms all incoming voice traffic is securely reaching your mobile handset.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: That gives me immense relief so the children's services team can reach me.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: I will also apply a twenty-pound goodwill credit to your telephone account for the inconvenience caused.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Thank you, the divert and credit resolve the immediate emergency.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Our broadband line to your premises remains stable with full fiber sync speed.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Our broadband internet has been working fine throughout, it was strictly the landline incoming calls.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: The emergency divert ticket reference logged on your account is DIV-88102-E.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Noted down... DIV-88102-E.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: I have verified that the emergency divert is active and tested, the twenty-pound credit is applied, and your foster care communication line is protected. Does that resolve the immediate issue for you today?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Yes Ian, the mobile diversion works and I can receive emergency foster placements now. Thank you.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Thank you for choosing S-Net today. Take care and have a good day. Goodbye.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Thank you Ian, goodbye.
